title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The external device (EE2) shares its live GPS coordinates with the backend (P1) without any authentication or encryption, making the data accessible to any entity that can intercept the transmission.

title: Data Linking and Identification
description: The transmission of GPS coordinates contains meta-data about the parties involved (the device and the backend), which can be used to link or identify the specific user and their location context.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The backend (P1) receives and stores the GPS coordinates, which may be used to track the user's movements, infer sensitive personal information, or create a persistent profile of the user's location history.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: The mobile app (P1) shares location data with the backend (P1) without explicit user consent or a valid privacy policy, allowing the backend to access sensitive location information.

title: Data Exfiltration or Misuse
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives the location data and stores it in a way that allows for unauthorized access, sharing, or deletion by unauthorized parties.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (P1) shares raw location coordinates with the backend (P1) without any user consent or explicit permission to share this sensitive personal information.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The mobile app (P1) processes the raw location data by transmitting it to the backend, which may store it in a way that allows for future profiling or targeted advertising.

title: Geofencing Logic Execution
description: The geofencing engine (P2) executes the logic to determine if a location is within a specific zone, which may reveal the user's precise location at the exact moment of the ping.

title: Unauthorized Access to Family Account
description: The source element (DataStore) shares data (zone definitions) with the destination element (Geofencing Engine) without explicit, granular permission controls. This allows the destination to access sensitive user data (home, school, friend's house) that the source owner may not intend to be publicly or broadly accessible.
assumptions: The system assumes the DataStore owner has broad administrative rights to share data with any external process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the DataStore owner has specific permissions to share zone definitions with external processes. This is a common default in many systems.

title: Data Processing for Unidentified Purpose
description: The destination element (Geofencing Engine) processes the shared data (zone definitions) to perform geofencing. This processing is not explicitly linked to a specific, authorized purpose for the data, creating a risk of misuse or unintended data usage.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine assumes the zone definitions are valid and necessary for its function, without verifying the specific purpose of the data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the Geofencing Engine has a specific, documented purpose for processing zone definitions. It may be used for a purpose not explicitly stated in the data sharing agreement.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: The parent entity (EE1) may access the arrival/departure notification data without explicit authorization or a valid reason, leading to potential misuse of the child's location information.
assumptions: The parent has not been granted specific permissions for this data flow.

title: Data Misuse or Disclosure
description: Upon receiving the notification, the parent entity (EE1) may use the arrival/departure data to identify the child entity and link it to other data sources, potentially violating privacy policies.
assumptions: The parent entity has not been informed of the data's sensitive nature.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity information (e.g., name, DOB, school) with the mobile app backend (P1) during the registration process. This creates a risk that the parent's identity is known to the app, potentially allowing the app to link or identify the parent's other data or future interactions.
assumptions: The parent entity is willing to share its identity with the backend.

title: Data Linking via Meta-data
description: The data flow itself transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., the parent's identity and the mobile app's identity) in transit. This allows the mobile app to link the parent's identity to the app's identity, which could be used to identify the parent's other data or future interactions.
assumptions: The parent entity is willing to share its identity with the backend.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the parent's identity and processes/stores it in a way that causes a threat. For example, the app might store the parent's identity in a way that allows it to be used to identify the parent's other data or future interactions, or the app might use the parent's identity to link to other data it holds.
assumptions: The parent entity is willing to share its identity with the backend.

title: Data Collection
description: The mobile app collects account, child profile, and geofence zone data from the user without explicit, informed consent.
assumptions: The app has the necessary permissions to access these data types.

title: Data Minimization
description: The app collects more data than necessary for the stated purpose (e.g., storing child profile data for a parent account).
assumptions: The data collected is strictly required for the app's functionality.

title: Data Retention
description: The app retains the collected data indefinitely or for an extended period without a clear legal basis.
assumptions: The retention policy is compliant with applicable laws.

title: Data Linking
description: The backend uses the mobile app's unique identifier to link the data flow to the user's identity, creating a profile.
assumptions: The app does not use other identifiers to link the data.

title: Data Association
description: The backend associates the collected data with the user's account, enabling targeted advertising or profiling.
assumptions: The data is not used for any purpose other than the stated app functionality.

title: Data Processing
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store processes the data in a way that allows for unauthorized access or modification.
assumptions: The store has appropriate access controls and encryption.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its child's location data with the mobile app backend without explicit consent or a valid legal basis for sharing personal location information.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) processes the parent's request to view location history, which may involve storing, aggregating, or re-identifying the parent's location data.

title: Location History Exposure
description: The source element (DataStore) shares location history data with the backend process. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to the recipient, potentially allowing the recipient to link or identify the data owner (the parent) with the data itself.
assumptions: The parent application has access to the backend API and the data is not encrypted or anonymized before transmission.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The destination element (Process) receives the location history data and processes it to serve the parent's map/history view. This action causes the threat because the data is stored and potentially used for personalization or profiling, which can lead to re-identification of the data owner.
assumptions: The backend process does not perform any additional data minimization or anonymization steps before serving the data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity with the mobile app backend (P1) to facilitate the invitation process. This disclosure allows the backend to identify the parent as a specific individual, which is necessary for the secondary guardian to be identified and invited.
assumptions: The parent trusts the backend to handle the invitation request securely.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow transmits meta-data about the parties involved (EE1 and the secondary guardian) to the backend. This meta-data allows the backend to link the parent's identity to the secondary guardian's identity, enabling the backend to identify the secondary guardian as a specific individual.
assumptions: The backend processes this meta-data to perform the identity linking.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the parent's identity and the secondary guardian's identity. The backend processes this data to identify the secondary guardian, which may lead to the parent's location data being accessed or shared with the secondary guardian in a way that is not intended.
assumptions: The backend processes the received data to identify the secondary guardian.

title: Unauthorized Access to Live Location Data
description: The backend process (P1) shares the child's live location data with the secondary guardian (EE3) without explicit, granular consent for this specific purpose. This creates a risk that the guardian could access, misuse, or leak the live location data.
assumptions: The backend process has the capability to share live location data.
uncertainty_note: Confident that the backend shares data, but the specific granularity of consent for live location sharing is not explicitly detailed in the flow description.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing by Secondary Guardian
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) receives the live location data and may process it in ways that cause privacy threats, such as storing it, sharing it with third parties, or using it for non-consensual purposes.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has the capability to process the received data.
uncertainty_note: Confident that the guardian processes data, but the specific processing actions are not defined in the flow description.

title: Data Sharing of Sensitive Usage Data
description: The source element (Backend) shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an external advertising/analytics partner. This data is highly sensitive as it contains personally identifiable information (PII) and behavioral data that could be used to identify, track, and profile users across the ecosystem.
assumptions: The backend system has the necessary technical capability to transmit this data securely, but the act of sharing itself exposes the data to potential misuse.

title: Data-Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow itself carries meta-data about the parties involved (Backend and EE4). This metadata, such as the names of the entities or the specific data types being exchanged, can be used to link or identify the parties, even if the actual data payload is encrypted.
assumptions: The metadata is not encrypted or obfuscated in a way that prevents third parties from identifying the source and destination entities.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing by Partner
description: The destination element (Advertising/Analytics Partner) receives the data and processes it in a way that causes a threat. The partner may use the data for targeted advertising, which could lead to the collection of additional PII or the creation of profiles that are not authorized by the user.
assumptions: The partner's internal systems are not sufficiently secured to prevent unauthorized access or misuse of the shared analytics data.

title: Location Disclosure
description: The child entity (EE2) shares its current location with the parent entity (P1) via a manual check-in/SOS message. This action exposes the child's precise location to the parent, potentially enabling the parent to track or monitor the child's movements.
assumptions: The child is aware of the parent's identity and intent to share location data.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The parent entity (P1) receives the location data and stores it in a way that allows for future tracking or profiling of the child. This processing may involve aggregating location data over time or correlating it with other personal information.
assumptions: The parent entity has the capability to store and process the received location data.
